model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP earnings ex acquisition charges after regulatory capital retention, deposits and borrowings not net debt, preferred stock deducted at par)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total revenue = 9M-2026 actual 9,382 (NII 6,420 + noninterest income 2,962, Q3-2026 10-Q income statement) + Q4-2026E ~3,370 (NII 2,271 x ~1.03 per the Q4 guide of +2.5-3.5% on the Q3 FTE base = ~2,340; fees ~1,030 against 1,059 in Q2 and 1,008 in Q3). NII lands inside the July guide (8.74-8.80bn); fees land ~1% under its 4.06-4.16bn range, partly the -32 of merger-related losses booked in noninterest income. Prior version used the guidance midpoint 12,880. FY2026 carries eleven months of Comerica (closed 1 Feb 2026); FY2025 standalone was 9,017. Q4-2026E annualised is ~13.5bn, which is the run-rate FY2027 grows from. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027 one period from the valuation date, which the engine's end-of-year discounting requires.
inputs.share_count_basis: 903.65m common shares outstanding at 31 Oct 2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) plus 5m dilutive share-based awards (Q3-2026 EPS note) = 908.6m, rounded to 909m. 30 Sep 2026 balance-sheet count was 907.37m; the 3.7m fall in October is the first evidence of the open-market buyback resuming (9M-2026 repurchases under the programme were nil; 93.07m shares remain authorised). Q3-2026 diluted weighted average was 917.1m. Held FLAT: share-based compensation is expensed in the flows and the buyback is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat, not an additional credit.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. Deposits ($239.5bn at 30 Sep 2026) and long-term debt ($16.9bn; total_debt above, recorded for audit only) are operating funding of an OCC/Fed-regulated bank whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and interest-bearing deposits with banks are held against that funding and are not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (earnings less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the CET1 target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. Preferred stock is the one claim that ranks ahead of common and is not inside NII: it is deducted at liquidation preference through equity_bridge.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE before preferred = earnings ex merger charges ~3,880 (12,750 x (42.3% - 1.55% SBC - 1.75% CDI amortisation) x (1 - 22%)) + CDI amortisation add-back ~235 (9M 171 + Q4 63) - capital retained ~1,625 (CET1 catch-up from 10.02% to ~10.25% on $249.3bn RWA ~570 + organic RWA growth ~4% x CET1 capital ~25.5bn ~1,020 + rounding). FY2026E margin 42.3% blends Q2 41.7% and Q3 43.6% on the same basis (Q3: pretax 1,108 + merger charges 225 + SBC 38 + CDI 63 = 1,434 on revenue 3,289 ex the -10 merger loss in fees). Cross-check on the reported side: Q3-2026 adjusted EPS $1.13 x 917m + 38 preferred = ~1,075 a quarter, ~4.3bn annualised on an unusually low provision (122, 3.7% of revenue). 9M-2026 GAAP net income 1,832 after 1,075 of pre-tax merger charges and the Q1 day-1 CECL provision. reported_fcf = FCFE + SBC so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 +4,514; Q1-2026 -1,106; Q2-2026 +2,796; Q3-2026 +835) is loan-sale, trading and deposit movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; free_cash_flow in the Metrics CSV is not used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: Stock-based compensation expense (cash-flow add-back): FY2024 164, FY2025 163, 9M-2026 226 of which Q1 145 (acceleration of Comerica awards at close), Q2 43, Q3 38. The post-close quarterly run-rate is ~$160-170m/yr (~1.25% of revenue); the 1.55% path is DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED because the charge is added to the margin and deducted again, so the house value is indifferent to it and only the street band narrows. Awards are net-share settled (341,595 shares withheld in Q3-2026); the withholding outflow is immaterial at this scale.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business (NII $8.7bn guided), and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: Repurchases of treasury stock: FY2024 625, FY2025 525, 9M-2026 nil under the programme. CET1 reached 10.03% at 30 Sep 2026, inside the 10.0-10.5% target band, and the share count fell 3.7m between 30 Sep and 31 Oct 2026, so the regular buyback appears to have resumed in Q4. The flat count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge in the flows; the capital-retention line (capex_pct_path) reserves the remaining CET1 build, and what is left after retention is distributable as dividends ($0.42/qtr, ~$1.5bn/yr) and buybacks.
inputs.book_value_anchor: Total equity $33,296m at 30 Sep 2026 less preferred stock $2,182m less goodwill $9,984m less intangibles $1,190m (CDI 1,057) = tangible common equity including AOCI $19,940m (Q3-2026 10-Q non-GAAP table) = $21.98/share on 907.4m, down from $23.23 at 30 Jun 2026 because other comprehensive loss was -1,652 in the quarter as long rates rose (AOCI -4,938). Tangible common equity EXCLUDING AOCI, the basis regulatory capital is measured on, is $24,878m = $27.42/share; CET1 10.03% on risk-weighted assets of $249,257m. Q3-2026 ROTCE 16.6% GAAP (after 225 of merger charges) on average TCE of 20,959; ~21% adjusted. Price/TBV is ~2.4x including AOCI and ~1.9x excluding it.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year Treasury ~5.07% (CBOE ^TNX, 18 Nov 2026; unchanged from ~5.1% at the prior valuation) + beta 1.1 x US equity risk premium 4.5% = 10.0%. UNCHANGED. Beta 1.1 for a top-10 super-regional with a commercially weighted book. One rate across all three scenarios; integration, credit-cycle and rate risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium. A normalised 4.5% risk-free would give 9.5% (see sensitivity grid).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branches, offices) are immaterial relative to equity and their cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest. Preferred dividends (~$150m/yr; 113 in 9M-2026, 38 in Q3) are NOT deducted from the flows; instead the preferred stock is deducted at its $2,182m liquidation preference in equity_bridge, which is the larger (more conservative) of the two treatments and avoids charging the preferred twice.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine; same model as the 2026-09-28 valuation (as NAB.AX, IAG.AX). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = g x required capital is the clean-surplus equivalent (FCFE = NI x (1 - g/ROTE)) and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income ex merger charges PLUS share-based compensation PLUS core-deposit-intangible amortisation, as % of revenue (Q2-2026 41.7%, Q3-2026 43.6%); sbc_pct_path = 1.55%; da_pct_path = CDI amortisation on the filed schedule (Q3-2026 10-Q: 2027 222, 2028 194, 2029 167, 2030 137, 2031 113, identical to the schedule used before), deducted before tax and added back after; capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the CET1 target plus the FY2027 CET1 catch-up; cash_tax_rate_path = 22% (9M-2026 effective 22.0%; cash taxes paid are far lower because of tax-credit investments whose cost sits in noninterest expense, so the GAAP rate is the economic rate); wacc = cost of equity 10.0%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = -2,182 preferred at par. UPDATE 2026-11-19 (Q3-2026 10-Q, balance sheet 30 Sep 2026). CHANGED: (1) anchors: FY0 revenue 12,880 -> 12,750 with year-1 growth re-based so FY2027 revenue is unchanged (base 13.65bn), shares 911m -> 909m, price and dates; (2) base FY2027 margin 42.7 -> 43.2: the Comerica systems conversion finished in Q3-2026, 1,075 of the ~1.3bn of merger charges is already booked and the rest falls in Q4-2026, so the trailing-integration-charge allowance in FY2027 is dropped (efficiency 55.5% -> 55.0%); (3) METHOD CORRECTION to the retention coefficient: the prior version sized retention on tangible common equity including AOCI (21.1bn, 1.64 x g) and inferred RWA of ~$216bn; reported RWA is $249.3bn (Q2 246.8bn) and CET1 capital is ~$25bn because the AOCI loss is excluded from regulatory capital, so holding CET1 at ~10.25% takes g x 25.5bn = ~2.0 x g of revenue. This is the largest mover, about -$2.2/share. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: all growth rates after year 1, all margins after year 1 in the base and every bull and bear margin, the provision path (5.5-6% of revenue; Q3's 3.7% is not extrapolated), SBC%, CDI path, tax rate, cost of equity, terminal growth and the 25/50/25 weights. What would move them: a full year at the $850m synergy run-rate with efficiency below 54% (base margins up); net charge-offs leaving the 30-40bp guide (provision path); a 10-year back under 4.5% (cost of equity 9.5%); Category III capital rules bringing AOCI into CET1 (retention up further). Residual-income cross-check: on CET1-basis tangible equity of $27.42/share at ROTE ~16% (4.1bn to common on 24.9bn), P/TBV = (16 - 2.5)/(10 - 2.5) = 1.8x = ~$49/share, in line with the engine base. Price is the NYSE regular close of 18 Nov 2026, not an after-hours print.

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock at liquidation preference (Series H/I/J/K/L plus Comerica series assumed)
equity_bridge.note: PreferredStockValue $2,182m at 30 Jun 2026, Q2-2026 10-Q. Deducted at par instead of stripping ~$150m/yr of preferred dividends from the flows; the two are not both applied.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is net income: FY2020 1,427 (COVID provisioning trough, provision 1,148); FY2021 2,770; FY2022 2,446; FY2023 2,349; FY2024 2,314; FY2025 2,522. The 5-year CAGR (12.1%) measures recovery from the FY2020 trough, not trend; the 3-year (1.0%) measures a flat standalone bank with NII squeezed by 2023-24 deposit betas. Revenue (NII + fees, Metrics CSV): FY2020 7,612; FY2022 8,375; FY2025 9,017; FY2026E 12,880 on eleven months of Comerica. All pre-merger CAGRs describe the standalone bank; the combined bank has one full quarter of history (Q2-2026).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth after FY2027 (4.0% fading to 2.5%), anchored on the standalone 5-year revenue CAGR (3.4%); FY2027 itself carries a twelfth month of Comerica (+~2pp) on top of organic growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (-1.2%) diverges >30% from revenue (3.4%) and EPS (14.1%): book value was hit by the 2022 AOCI mark on the securities book (equity fell 22,210 -> 17,327 in FY2022) and then jumped 59% in Q1-2026 on the all-stock Comerica issuance, so equity CAGR does not describe the earnings power. EPS 5-year CAGR is measured from the FY2020 COVID trough ($1.84). Growth is taken from the revenue series and management's FY2026 guidance.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 7.0% on the FY2026E base of 12,750 = FY2027 revenue ~13.65bn, the same level as the prior version (6.0% on 12,880): a twelfth month of Comerica plus ~3.5% organic, and ~1.2% above the Q4-2026E annualised run-rate of ~13.5bn. Then 4.0% tapering to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP less structural NIM compression), in line with the standalone 3.4% 5-year revenue CAGR plus the Southeast/Sun Belt de novo programme (50+ branches/yr to 2028). Years 2-10 unchanged.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax ex merger charges + SBC + CDI amortisation, on revenue. FY2027 43.2% = 100 - efficiency 55.0% - provision 5.5% + SBC 1.55 + CDI 1.65 (rounded); raised from 42.7% because merger charges end in FY2026 (systems conversion done in Q3-2026, ~1.3bn total of which 1,075 booked by 30 Sep). Q3-2026 printed 43.6% on a 3.7% provision and before the full $850m run-rate, so 43.2% with a 5.5% provision still assumes most of the remaining synergy is reinvested in 50+ branches a year and technology. Years 2-10 unchanged: provision rising to 6.0% mature (~43bp of loans), efficiency ~55%, CDI running off to ~40.6.
base.da_rationale: Core deposit intangible amortisation on the filed schedule (222 / 194 / 167 / 137 / 113 for the next five years, Q2-2026 10-Q) over projected revenue, running off to ~0.1% by year 10. Non-cash, book-only (an all-stock reorganisation carries no tax step-up), added back after tax; the ~$50m/yr tax shield the engine implies on the deduction is the only simplification and is inside the 22% rate's rounding.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at ~10.25% as RWA grows with revenue = g x CET1 capital / revenue = ~2.0 x g (10.25% x $249.3bn RWA = 25.5bn on FY2026E revenue 12.75bn). FY2027 11.6% (~$1.59bn) = 4% organic RWA growth (~$1,020m; the extra Comerica month needs no new capital) plus a ~$570m catch-up from 10.03% to ~10.25%. Thereafter 8.0% at 4% growth falling to 5.0% at 2.5% terminal growth, i.e. ~83% of earnings distributable at maturity. Prior version used 1.64 x g on tangible common equity including AOCI; regulatory capital excludes the AOCI loss, so the required capital base is larger.

bull.growth_rationale: Comerica's middle-market and specialty commercial franchise and the Southeast/Texas branch build compound loans at 5-6% with NIM widening as the deposit book reprices down faster than assets; wealth fees grow high-single-digit on ~$690bn assets under care. Revenue +9% FY2027 on the 12,750 base (same FY2027 level as before: twelfth Comerica month plus ~5.5% organic) fading to 3% terminal. Years 2-10 unchanged.
bull.margin_rationale: Efficiency ratio reaches 52% by FY2029 (full $850m synergies plus operating leverage on a larger base; Q2-2026 already 57%) and credit stays benign at ~5% of revenue (~35bp): 100 - 52 - 5 + 1.55 + CDI. Held at ~45.5 as CDI runs off.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = ~2.0 x g on CET1 capital (see base): faster growth needs more capital even at a higher return. FY2027 14.2% includes the same ~$570m CET1 catch-up. Terminal 3% growth retains 6.0% of revenue.

bear.growth_rationale: Higher-for-longer rates (10-year above 5%) compress NIM as deposit costs stay sticky while loan demand stalls; Comerica customer attrition after the systems conversion offsets the twelfth month of contribution (FY2027 +3% on the 12,750 base, the same FY2027 level as before and ~2.5% BELOW the Q4-2026E run-rate); a 2027-28 credit downturn in commercial real estate and leveraged middle-market lending keeps loan growth near zero. Revenue then grows 0.5-2%. Years 2-10 unchanged.
bear.margin_rationale: Provision at 8% of revenue in FY2027 and 10% in FY2028 (~60-75bp NCO; FY2020 was 15%, FY2009 far worse) with efficiency drifting to 57.5% on synergy slippage, retention spend and integration overruns. FY2027: 100 - 57.5 - 8.0 + 1.55 SBC + 1.7 CDI = 37.8, taken at 36.2 to carry ~$200m of trailing integration charges; FY2028: 100 - 57.5 - 10.0 + 1.55 + 1.45 = 35.5, taken at 34.9. Recovers to provision 6.5% and efficiency 56.5% by year 6: 100 - 56.5 - 6.5 + 1.55 + CDI 0.6 = 39.2, held at 38.7 as CDI runs off with fees recovering 1pp.
bear.capex_rationale: Prior bear path scaled by 2.0/1.64 for the CET1-capital base (see base). Retention stays well above 2.0 x g in FY2027-29 despite 0.5-2% growth because RWA migration in a downturn consumes capital and the CET1 build still has to be funded; buybacks are suspended for two years. Terminal 2% growth retains 4.0% of revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: Fifth Third has Comerica converted: systems conversion finished in Q3-2026, the $850m synergy run-rate is in place for Q4-2026 and merger charges end with FY2026, but most of the saving is reinvested in 50+ Southeast and Texas branches a year and technology, so the efficiency ratio settles around 55% rather than the low 50s. Revenue reaches ~$13.65bn in FY2027 on a twelfth month of Comerica and ~3.5% organic, then growth fades to 2.5%. Credit normalises from today's ~30bp to ~40bp of loans on a book that is now ~60% commercial. CET1 is built from 10.03% to the middle of the 10.0-10.5% band in FY2027 and thereafter ~80-85% of earnings is distributed through the $0.42 quarterly dividend and buybacks. At a 10% cost of equity the bank is worth a little under the market price: fair value, not a bargain.
scenario_narratives.bull: Comerica's middle-market, specialty commercial and Texas/California footprint compounds faster than the Midwest core, the Southeast de novo programme keeps taking deposit share, and the deposit book reprices down faster than assets so NIM widens. Full synergies plus operating leverage take the efficiency ratio to 52% by FY2029 with credit still benign (~35bp). Earnings reach ~$5.5bn by FY2029 and the bank distributes most of it; a 3% terminal growth rate on a 45% pre-tax margin is worth materially more than today's price.
scenario_narratives.bear: Customer and deposit attrition follows the Comerica conversion and the synergy run-rate leaks into retention spend. At the same time the 5%+ 10-year, which already cost $1.65bn of AOCI in Q3-2026, proves durable: deposit costs stay sticky, loan demand stalls, and a 2027-28 credit turn in commercial real estate and leveraged middle-market lending lifts the provision to 8-10% of revenue (60-75bp NCO). Buybacks are suspended for two years while CET1 is rebuilt through retained earnings. Growth settles at 2% and the pre-tax margin recovers only to ~37%, leaving the bank worth about a quarter below today's price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25 (house default 15/50/35). Evidence since September cuts both ways: the systems conversion is complete and CET1 is back inside the band, which lowers integration risk, but the 10-year is still above 5%, Q3-2026 took a $1.65bn AOCI loss, NIM slipped 2bp and the buyback has only just restarted. Bear stays at 25% until a full year of combined results shows deposit retention and the synergy run-rate holding; bull stays at 25% because it needs synergy overshoot, NIM expansion, Sun Belt share gains and benign credit all to hold for a decade.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A super-regional bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity, never on statutory operating cash flow and never with deposits or senior debt treated as net debt. Earnings ex merger charges are the flow, the core-deposit-intangible amortisation is added back because it is book-only, capital retention at the CET1 target on reported risk-weighted assets is the reinvestment, preferred stock is deducted at par, and 10% is the return an owner requires with the 10-year at 5%. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: the franchise is worth roughly what the market pays, so the stock is a fair-value hold rather than a bargain, and the 15% hurdle entry price sits far below the quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Synergy retention: every 10% of the $850m run-rate competed or reinvested away is ~$65m after tax (~1.6% of earnings); attrition on the Comerica commercial deposit book would hit NII directly
Credit cycle: every 10bp on the provision (on ~$181bn of loans) is ~$180m pre-tax (~4.5% of earnings); FY2020 provisioning was 15% of revenue versus the 5.5-6% modelled and Q3-2026's 3.7%
Net interest margin: 5bp on ~$270bn of interest-earning assets is ~$135m of NII (1% of revenue); NIM fell 2bp in Q3-2026 and the Q4 NII guide depends on the Fed path
Cost of equity: the 10.0% rate embeds a ~5.1% 10-year; one point either way is roughly $6-7/share in the base case (sensitivity grid)

Capital: retention is sized on CET1 at ~10.25% of $249bn RWA with the $4.9bn AOCI loss excluded; Category III treatment above $250bn of assets or a Basel endgame that pulls AOCI into CET1 would raise required capital materially
Share count: 909m is the 31 Oct 2026 count plus 5m dilutive awards; the restarted buyback will lower it but the model gives no credit beyond what is in a filing

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 40.98-59.50.
data_sources.financials: FITB_Metrics.csv / FITB.duckdb core_metrics and kpis through Q3-2026 (CET1Ratio, RiskWeightedAssets, ROTCE, NetInterestIncome, NonInterestIncome, buybacks, cash_taxes); FITB_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (10-Q for 30 Sep 2026): income statement, equity statement, non-GAAP tangible-equity table, regulatory capital table, merger-related charges note, intangible amortisation schedule, share repurchase table and cover share count; FY2025 10-K for annual history.
data_sources.qualitative: FITB_Analysis.json (2026-11-19): Q3-2026 results, Comerica systems conversion and $850m synergy run-rate, ~$1.3bn total merger charges, Q4-2026 NII and loan guidance, CET1 target, analyst targets, bull/bear cases.
